logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of the ruthenium(II) complexes was determined using the shake-flask technique37 with 1-octanol and PBS (150 mm sodium chloride, 10 mm sodium phosphate, pH 7.4). PBS buffer is generally considered a more appropriate model of blood serum than pure water, as it better approximates the ionic strength and pH of blood plasma. The solute (33.3×10-5 m) was dissolved first in octanol and PBS, then the two saturated phases were shaken for 30 min at room temperature, and then let to equilibrate for 24 h. After this period, the distribution of the complex in each solvent was measured using a Hewlett–Packard HP8453A spectrophotometer. The corresponding concentration of the solute in each solvent was determined using Beer's law from the absorbance of the measured spectra; the concentration was then used in calculating the partition coefficient. The partition coefficient (Po/w) is the ratio of the equilibrium concentration of the dissolved compound in two phases [Eq. 1]: logPo/w = log([solute]octanol / [solute]water). The logP of the ruthenium complexes was also obtained for a biphasic solution of DI water and 1-octanol using the same general procedure above.
